beats: Congratulations! Your new website is ready, and it's one hundred percent yours.
In this video, we'll put it online together. It takes about ten minutes, it's free, and you don't need any tech skills.
There are four simple steps. Unzip your website. Put it on Netlify. Get your own web address. And connect the two.

title: Your two files
caption: Use the “website” file · Keep the “code” file as a backup
check: You've found both files in your email
beats: First, open the email with your website. It has two files attached.
The one ending in website, is your website. That's the one we'll use today.
The one ending in code, is your backup. Save it somewhere safe, like Google Drive. If you ever hire someone to change your site, give them that file.

title: Unzip your website
caption: Windows: right-click → Extract All   ·   Mac: double-click
check: You see a yellow folder called yourbusiness-website
beats: Your website arrives zipped up, like a parcel. Let's open it.
On Windows, right-click the website file. Click Extract All. Then click Extract.
On a Mac, just double-click it.
Now you'll see a normal folder with the same name. That folder is your website.

title: Create your free Netlify account
caption: netlify.com  →  Sign up  →  use your business email
check: You're logged in to your own Netlify account
beats: Next, your website needs a home on the internet. We'll use Netlify. It hosts millions of websites, and it's free for a site like yours.
Go to netlify dot com, and click Sign up.
Type in your business email, and click Sign up. Then open your inbox, and click Confirm.
If it asks a few questions, answer them, or skip. That's it. The account is yours, in your name.

title: Put your website online
caption: app.netlify.com/drop  →  drag in your FOLDER
check: Your link ending in .netlify.app opens your website
beats: Now the fun part. While you're logged in, go to app dot netlify dot com, slash drop.
You'll see a box that says drag and drop. Grab the folder you unzipped. The folder, not the zip file. And drop it in the box.
Wait a few seconds.
And that's it. Your website is live on the internet!
Netlify gives it a temporary address, ending in netlify dot app. Click it to have a look.

title: Get your own web address
caption: Buy it in YOUR name  ·  Turn ON auto-renew
check: Domain bought in your name, with auto-renew ON
beats: Right now your site has a temporary address. Let's give it your own, like your business dot com dot au. This is called a domain.
It costs around fifteen to twenty five dollars a year. You buy it in your own name, so it's yours.
We'll use Namecheap. GoDaddy and Cloudflare work the same way. Type the name you want, and click Search. If it's available, click Add to cart, then Checkout.
Important. Turn auto-renew on. If a domain isn't renewed, your address stops working.
Australian dot com dot au names need an A B N, so have yours ready. Already own a domain? Just log in to where you bought it.

title: Connect your domain
caption: Copy 4 nameservers from Netlify  →  paste into “Custom DNS”
check: 4 nameservers saved at your domain company
beats: Now let's point your new address at your website. In Netlify, open your site, and click Domain management.
Click Add a domain. Type your domain exactly as you bought it. Click Verify, then Add domain.
Netlify offers to manage your domain. Choose Netlify D N S, and click Continue until you see four nameservers. Keep this page open.
Now, in a new tab, open Namecheap. Go to Domain List, and click Manage next to your domain.
Find Nameservers, and change it to Custom D N S.
Copy each of the four nameservers from Netlify, and paste them in, one per line. Then click the green tick to save.
Using GoDaddy or Cloudflare? Look for the same word. Nameservers.

title: You're live
caption: Can take up to 24 hours  ·  The padlock appears by itself
beats: That's everything! Now the internet needs a little time to catch up. Usually a few minutes to a few hours, sometimes up to a day. That's completely normal.
Netlify adds the security padlock all by itself, once your domain is connected.
When you type in your address and your website appears, you're live!
Your website, your hosting, and your domain are all in your name. Congratulations, and thank you for your business!
Here's your checklist.
